title: Fugue in C-sharp minor
blurb: Ten of the twelve entries land before bar 32, four of them two bars apart. Then the subject disappears for twenty-nine bars and comes back twice at the end.
card: The only fugue here in 12/16, and it drops the subject for twenty-nine bars in the middle.
history: Nineteen notes inside a bar and a half of 12/16, which is a dancing subject however you play it. Bach spends the first half of the piece stacking it up — entries at bars 24, 26, 28 and 30, three of the twelve turned upside down — and then stops. From bar 32 to bar 61 there is no complete statement anywhere. The next longest gap in the piece is nine bars.
The prelude is in 9/8 and covered in mordents and appoggiaturas; the fugue has almost none. Two pieces in compound time sitting next to each other, with all the decoration in one of them.

Book II was put together in Leipzig around 1739–42, nearly twenty years after Book I, out of pieces Bach had been writing over a much longer span. The main source is the London autograph in the British Library, some of it in his hand, some in Anna Magdalena's.
